questions.subject: Economy
questions.question: Which one of the following statements best describes the term 'Core Inflation'?

options.a: It is the overall inflation rate measured through the Consumer Price Index (CPI).
options.b: It is the inflation rate excluding food and fuel components from headline inflation.
options.c: It is the inflation rate based exclusively on the Wholesale Price Index (WPI).
options.d: It is the inflation rate observed during an economic depression.

questions.concept: Measuring persistent price pressures by stripping volatile supply-shock items.
questions.explanation: Headline inflation (CPI Combined) captures price changes across all consumer goods including volatile items like vegetables, fruit, pulses, petrol, and diesel. 'Core Inflation' strips out the highly volatile food and energy/fuel segments to capture underlying long-term inflationary trends driven by generalized demand-side pressures.

optionAnalysis.a: Incorrect: That describes Headline Inflation (CPI-C).
optionAnalysis.b: Correct: Core inflation = Headline CPI minus (Food and Beverages + Fuel and Light).
optionAnalysis.c: Incorrect: Core inflation is derived from CPI or WPI by stripping volatile items, not exclusively from WPI.
optionAnalysis.d: Incorrect: Deflation or disinflation characterizes severe depressions.

questions.trap: Confusing 'Headline' (total overall CPI basket) with 'Core' (stripped of food and fuel volatility).
relatedFacts: RBI's flexible inflation targeting framework (Urjit Patel Committee) targets CPI Combined at 4% with a tolerance band of +/- 2%.
In India, Food and Beverages carry approximately 45.86% weight in the CPI Combined basket.
Refined Core Inflation also strips out transport and communication fuels.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.question: In the context of finance, the term 'Beta' refers to:

options.a: the process of simultaneous purchase and sale of an asset from different platforms
options.b: an investment strategy of a portfolio manager to balance risk versus reward
options.c: a type of systemic risk arising where perfect hedging is not possible
options.d: a numeric value that measures the fluctuations of a stock to changes in the overall stock market

questions.concept: Beta (β) as a statistical measure of volatility/systematic risk relative to a benchmark index.
questions.explanation: Beta (β) is a measure of a security's or portfolio's sensitivity and volatility in comparison to the broader market (e.g., Nifty 50 or Sensex). A beta of 1 indicates the stock moves in tandem with the market; beta > 1 signifies greater volatility than the market, while beta < 1 signifies lower volatility.

optionAnalysis.a: Incorrect: That describes Arbitrage.
optionAnalysis.b: Incorrect: That describes Asset Allocation or Portfolio Balancing.
optionAnalysis.c: Incorrect: That refers to residual or unhedged risk.
optionAnalysis.d: Correct: Standard financial definition of Beta coefficient.

questions.trap: Arbitrage vs Beta: Option (a) is a classic distractor for arbitrage transactions.
relatedFacts: Alpha (α) measures an investment's performance relative to a benchmark index (excess returns generated by manager skill).
Sharpe Ratio measures risk-adjusted return relative to risk-free treasury rate.
Systematic risk cannot be diversified away, whereas unsystematic (idiosyncratic) risk can be mitigated through diversification.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.question: With reference to Inflation-Indexed Bonds (IIBs), consider the following statements:
statements: Government can reduce the coupon rates on its borrowing by way of IIBs.
IIBs provide protection to the investors from uncertainty regarding inflation.
The interest received as well as capital gains on IIBs are not taxable.
questions.concept: Principal and coupon adjustments linked to CPI to protect real purchasing power.
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is correct: Because IIBs insulate investors against inflation risk, investors accept a lower nominal coupon rate (real yield), thereby lowering government borrowing costs. Statement 2 is correct: Both the principal and periodic coupon payments are adjusted to consumer price inflation, eliminating inflation uncertainty. Statement 3 is incorrect: The interest received and capital gains on IIBs are subject to normal tax rules (no complete tax exemption).

statementAnalysis.text: Government can reduce the coupon rates on its borrowing by way of IIBs.
statementAnalysis.why: Real yields offered are lower than nominal bond coupons.

statementAnalysis.text: IIBs provide protection to the investors from uncertainty regarding inflation.
statementAnalysis.why: Principal value is indexed to inflation (WPI/CPI).

statementAnalysis.text: The interest received as well as capital gains on IIBs are not taxable.
statementAnalysis.why: Interest and capital gains are subject to standard income tax provisions.

optionAnalysis.a: Correct: Statements 1 and 2 are true, while statement 3 falsely asserts tax immunity.
optionAnalysis.b: Incorrect because statement 3 is false.
optionAnalysis.c: Incorrect because statement 3 is false.

questions.trap: UPSC frequently uses false blanket tax exemption claims ('are not taxable') as trap statements.
relatedFacts: RBI first issued IIBs in 2013 linked to WPI, and subsequently linked them to CPI for retail investors.
Sovereign Gold Bonds (SGBs) enjoy capital gains tax exemption on redemption after maturity, unlike IIBs.
TIPS (Treasury Inflation-Protected Securities) is the equivalent American sovereign instrument.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.question: The money multiplier in an economy increases with which one of the following?

options.a: Increase in the Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) in the banks
options.b: Increase in the Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR) in the banks
options.c: Increase in the banking habit of the population
options.d: Increase in the population of the country

questions.concept: Inverse relationship between reserve/currency drain and credit creation (m = 1 / (c + r)).
questions.explanation: Money Multiplier (m) is the ratio of Broad Money (M3) to Reserve Money / High-Powered Money (M0). The money multiplier is given by m = (1 + c) / (c + r), where 'c' is the currency-deposit ratio and 'r' is the reserve-deposit ratio. When the banking habit of the population increases, people hold less physical cash and deposit more into commercial banks, reducing 'c'. This expands the loanable funds of the banking system and increases the credit-creation multiplier.

optionAnalysis.a: Incorrect: An increase in CRR locks away more reserves, decreasing the money multiplier.
optionAnalysis.b: Incorrect: An increase in SLR forces banks to hold more liquid assets, reducing credit creation and the multiplier.
optionAnalysis.c: Correct: Higher banking habits reduce the currency leak and maximize bank credit multiplication.
optionAnalysis.d: Incorrect: Mere population growth without banking habits does not expand the multiplier.

questions.trap: Students often assume CRR increases money creation, when in reality reserve requirements drain credit capacity.
relatedFacts: High-Powered Money (M0) = Currency in circulation + Bankers' deposits with RBI + 'Other' deposits with RBI.
Broad Money (M3) = Currency with public + Demand deposits + Time deposits with banking system.
Demonetization in 2016 led to a temporary spike in bank deposits, altering the currency-deposit ratio.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.question: If the RBI decides to adopt an expansionist monetary policy, which of the following would it NOT do?
statements: Cut and optimize the Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR)
Increase the Marginal Standing Facility (MSF) rate
Cut the Bank Rate and Repo Rate
questions.concept: Negative constraint question: identifying contractionary actions during monetary easing.
questions.explanation: An expansionist (dovish/accommodative) policy aims to inject liquidity and lower borrowing costs to stimulate growth. Actions 1 (cutting SLR) and 3 (cutting Bank Rate and Repo Rate) inject liquidity and are expansionary. Action 2 (increasing MSF rate) makes emergency borrowing expensive, absorbing liquidity, which is a CONTRACTIONARY measure. Hence, the RBI would NOT do Statement 2.

statementAnalysis.text: Cut and optimize the Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR)
statementAnalysis.why: This is an expansionist step (frees up loanable funds).

statementAnalysis.text: Increase the Marginal Standing Facility (MSF) rate
statementAnalysis.why: This is contractionary; RBI would NOT do this in an expansionist cycle.

statementAnalysis.text: Cut the Bank Rate and Repo Rate
statementAnalysis.why: This is an expansionist step (lowers cost of funds).

optionAnalysis.a: Incorrect: Statement 1 is expansionary.
optionAnalysis.b: Correct: Statement 2 is the only contractionary action that RBI would NOT undertake.
optionAnalysis.c: Incorrect: Statements 1 and 3 are standard expansionary actions.

questions.trap: Candidates miss the negative qualifier 'which of the following would it NOT do?' and select expansionary steps instead.
relatedFacts: Repo Rate is the policy rate under the Liquidity Adjustment Facility (LAF) where RBI lends against government securities with a repurchase agreement.
Standing Deposit Facility (SDF) replaced the reverse repo rate as the floor of the LAF corridor without requiring collateral.
The MSF rate forms the upper ceiling of the interest rate corridor.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding Purchasing Power Parity (PPP):
statements: The purchasing power parity (PPP) exchange rates are calculated by comparing the prices of the same basket of goods and services in different countries.
In terms of PPP dollars, India is the sixth largest economy in the world.
questions.subTopic: Purchasing Power Parity (PPP) vs Nominal GDP
questions.concept: Methodology of International Comparison Program (ICP) and relative economic size.
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is correct: PPP exchange rates equalize the purchasing power of different currencies by evaluating the cost of a standardized basket of identical goods and services (Law of One Price). Statement 2 is incorrect: In terms of PPP GDP, India is the THIRD largest economy in the world (behind China and the United States). India was fifth/sixth in nominal GDP terms, not PPP.

statementAnalysis.text: The purchasing power parity (PPP) exchange rates are calculated by comparing the prices of the same basket of goods and services in different countries.
statementAnalysis.why: Standard ICP methodology under the World Bank.

statementAnalysis.text: In terms of PPP dollars, India is the sixth largest economy in the world.
statementAnalysis.why: India is the 3rd largest economy in PPP terms (behind China and USA).

optionAnalysis.a: Correct: Statement 1 is valid, while statement 2 is factually incorrect.
optionAnalysis.b: Incorrect because statement 2 is false.
optionAnalysis.c: Incorrect because statement 2 is false.

questions.trap: Swapping rankings: 5th in Nominal GDP vs 3rd in PPP GDP.
relatedFacts: The Big Mac Index created by The Economist is an informal illustration of Purchasing Power Parity.
Because price levels of non-traded services (like haircuts, healthcare) are lower in developing countries, PPP GDP of developing nations is higher than their nominal market exchange rate GDP.
Penn World Table provides standardized national accounts across countries adjusted for PPP.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.question: Which one of the following statements is correct with reference to 'Legal Tender Money'?

options.a: The money which is tendered in courts of law to defray the fee of legal cases
options.b: The money which a creditor is under legal obligation to accept in satisfaction of claims
options.c: The bank money in the form of cheques, drafts, bills of exchange, etc.
options.d: The metallic money in circulation in a country

questions.concept: Statutory compulsion to accept currency notes and coins for settlement of debts under law.
questions.explanation: Legal tender is currency that has been declared by law to be valid for the payment of all debts, both public and private. Creditors are legally obligated to accept it in discharge of debt obligations; refusing valid legal tender without lawful excuse is an offence.

optionAnalysis.a: Incorrect: Literal wordplay on 'legal'.
optionAnalysis.b: Correct: Essential statutory definition of legal tender under Coinage Act and RBI Act Section 26.
optionAnalysis.c: Incorrect: Cheques and drafts are optional/fiduciary money, not legal tender.
optionAnalysis.d: Incorrect: Both paper currency notes and metallic coins constitute legal tender.

questions.trap: Options (a) and (c) create wordplay distractors around court legalities and commercial instruments.
relatedFacts: Section 26 of the RBI Act, 1934 provides that every banknote issued by the RBI shall be legal tender throughout India.
Coins up to Rs. 1,000 can be issued under Coinage Act, 2011; coins are limited legal tender (e.g. 50 paise up to Rs. 10; Rs. 1 and above up to Rs. 1,000).
Bank notes are unlimited legal tender guaranteed by the Central Government.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.question: With reference to the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC), consider the following statements:
statements: It decides the RBI's benchmark interest rates.
It is a 12-member body including the Governor of RBI and is reconstituted every year.
It functions under the chairmanship of the Union Finance Minister.
questions.subTopic: Monetary Policy Committee Framework (Section 45ZB RBI Act)
questions.concept: Institutional architecture for flexible inflation targeting established post-2016.
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is correct: The MPC decides the policy repo rate required to achieve the inflation target. Statement 2 is incorrect: Under Section 45ZB of the amended RBI Act 1934, the MPC consists of SIX members (3 from RBI, 3 external experts appointed by the Central Government), not 12. External members hold office for 4 years and are not eligible for reappointment. Statement 3 is incorrect: The Governor of the RBI is the ex-officio Chairperson of the MPC, NOT the Union Finance Minister.

statementAnalysis.text: It decides the RBI's benchmark interest rates.
statementAnalysis.why: Determines the policy Repo rate.

statementAnalysis.text: It is a 12-member body including the Governor of RBI and is reconstituted every year.
statementAnalysis.why: It has 6 members, not 12, with a 4-year tenure.

statementAnalysis.text: It functions under the chairmanship of the Union Finance Minister.
statementAnalysis.why: RBI Governor is the ex-officio Chairperson.

optionAnalysis.a: Correct: Only statement 1 is factually valid.
optionAnalysis.b: Incorrect because statement 2 is false.
optionAnalysis.c: Incorrect because statement 3 is false.
optionAnalysis.d: Incorrect because both statements 2 and 3 are false.

questions.trap: Examiners frequently replace the RBI Governor with the Union Finance Minister to test executive vs central bank autonomy.
relatedFacts: In case of a tie, the RBI Governor has a casting/second vote under Section 45ZL.
The MPC must meet at least four times a year, and each member's vote and rationale must be published after 14 days.
The statutory basis was introduced through the Finance Act, 2016.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.question: The term 'Core Banking Solutions' is sometimes seen in the news. Which of the following statements best describes this term?

options.a: It is a networking of a bank's branches which enables customers to operate their accounts from any branch.
options.b: It is an effort to increase RBI's control over commercial banks through computerized networks.
options.c: It is a procedure by which a bank with huge non-performing assets is taken over by another bank.
options.d: It is an automated procedure to sanction loans in rural areas without human intervention.

questions.concept: Centralized database architecture transitioning customer relationships from 'branch banking' to 'bank banking'.
questions.explanation: Core Banking Solutions (CBS) is a software platform where all branches of a commercial bank are connected to a central centralized database server. This allows real-time transaction processing so that a customer becomes a 'customer of the bank' rather than just a 'customer of a specific branch', permitting deposits, withdrawals, and fund transfers from any branch nationwide.

optionAnalysis.a: Correct: Definitional essence of CBS architecture.
optionAnalysis.b: Incorrect: CBS is an internal commercial bank operations network, not RBI surveillance.
optionAnalysis.c: Incorrect: That relates to Prompt Corrective Action (PCA) or bank mergers.

questions.trap: Conflating commercial bank operational networking with RBI central regulatory oversight.
relatedFacts: Finacle (by Infosys) and BaNCS (by TCS) are premier CBS software used globally.
CBS enabled the rollout of NEFT, RTGS, and IMPS instant payment rails.
Public sector banks completed 100% CBS implementation in the 2000s under RBI modernization directives.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.question: Convertibility of the rupee implies:

options.a: being able to convert rupee notes into gold
options.b: allowing the value of the rupee to be fixed by market forces
options.c: freely permitting the conversion of rupee to other currencies and vice versa
options.d: developing an international market for currencies in India

questions.concept: Absence of restrictions on foreign exchange transactions under Article VIII of IMF Articles of Agreement.
questions.explanation: Convertibility of a currency means that residents and non-residents are allowed to freely exchange domestic currency into foreign currencies (and vice versa) at market exchange rates without administrative restrictions or state permits.

optionAnalysis.a: Incorrect: That describes the historical Gold Standard.
optionAnalysis.b: Incorrect: That describes a floating exchange rate regime.
optionAnalysis.c: Correct: Precise economic definition of currency convertibility.
optionAnalysis.d: Incorrect: That refers to setting up an onshore financial exchange (like GIFT City IFSC).

questions.trap: Confusing 'market-determined exchange rate' with 'convertibility' (which is the freedom to exchange without restriction).
relatedFacts: India achieved full convertibility on the Current Account in August 1994 by accepting obligations under Article VIII of the IMF.
Capital Account Convertibility (CAC) in India remains partial; the Tarapore Committees (1997 and 2006) laid down preconditions.
Liberalised Remittance Scheme (LRS) allows Indian residents to remit up to $250,000 per financial year for permitted transactions.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.question: The terms 'Marginal Standing Facility' and 'Standing Liquidity Facility' are related to:
questions.concept: Overnight liquidity window for scheduled commercial banks to manage interbank liquidity shocks.
questions.explanation: Marginal Standing Facility (MSF) was introduced by the RBI in May 2011. It allows scheduled commercial banks to borrow overnight funds from the RBI up to an approved percentage of their Net Demand and Time Liabilities (NDTL) against government securities, at an interest rate higher than the repo rate, even dipping into their Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR) quota.

optionAnalysis.a: Correct: MSF is a specialized window in Indian banking operations.
optionAnalysis.b: Incorrect: Distractor.
optionAnalysis.c: Incorrect: Distractor.

questions.trap: Direct definition question designed to test awareness of post-2011 monetary reform vocabulary.
relatedFacts: Under MSF, banks can borrow funds overnight when inter-bank call money liquidity completely dries up.
Banks can dip up to a specified percentage (e.g. 2%) into their mandatory SLR securities to borrow under MSF.
The minimum MSF application amount is Rs. 1 crore and in multiples of Rs. 1 crore thereafter.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.question: Disguised unemployment generally means:

options.a: large number of people remain unemployed
options.c: marginal productivity of labour is zero

questions.concept: Arthur Lewis and Ragnar Nurkse's structural surplus labor concept in agrarian economies.
questions.explanation: Disguised unemployment (hidden unemployment) occurs when more people are engaged in an economic activity than are actually needed. If some workers are withdrawn from the work, total output remains completely unchanged; hence the marginal physical product of additional labor is zero (or near zero). This is a chronic structural feature of Indian agriculture.

optionAnalysis.a: Incorrect: That describes open unemployment.
optionAnalysis.b: Incorrect: Lack of alternative jobs is a cause, not the definition.
optionAnalysis.c: Correct: Exact theoretical definition formulated in economics by Joan Robinson and Ragnar Nurkse.
optionAnalysis.d: Incorrect: While average productivity may be low, the formal definition requires zero marginal productivity.

questions.trap: Confusing low average productivity (Option d) with zero marginal productivity (Option c).
relatedFacts: Frictional unemployment occurs during the transition time when workers search for or switch between jobs.
Structural unemployment arises from a mismatch between worker skills and the technological demands of new jobs.
Cyclical unemployment (Keynesian unemployment) results from deficient aggregate demand during an economic recession.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.question: With reference to Central Bank Digital Currencies (CBDC), consider the following statements:
statements: It is possible to make payments in a digital currency without using US dollar or SWIFT system.
A digital currency can be distributed with condition programmed into it such as a time-frame for spending it.
questions.concept: Sovereign programmable digital fiat currency on distributed ledger technology bypassing conventional correspondent banking.
questions.explanation: Both statements are correct: Statement 1 is correct: CBDCs allow direct peer-to-peer cross-border sovereign settlements between bilateral central banks (e.g. mBridge project, Project Nexus), completely bypassing the US dollar and SWIFT (Society for Worldwide Interbank Financial Telecommunication) messaging rail. Statement 2 is correct: Digital currencies support smart contracts and programmability; central banks can issue targeted purpose-bound or time-bound currency (e.g. agricultural input subsidies that expire if not redeemed within 90 days at fertilizer stores).

statementAnalysis.text: It is possible to make payments in a digital currency without using US dollar or SWIFT system.
statementAnalysis.why: Direct bilateral DLT corridors eliminate reliance on SWIFT messaging.

statementAnalysis.text: A digital currency can be distributed with condition programmed into it such as a time-frame for spending it.
statementAnalysis.why: Programmable smart contracts can embed expiration dates or designated vendor restrictions.

optionAnalysis.a: Incorrect because statement 2 is also true.
optionAnalysis.b: Incorrect because statement 1 is also true.
optionAnalysis.c: Correct option validating both technical capabilities of CBDCs.

questions.trap: Believing digital currencies cannot have expiration dates or spending conditions programmed into them.
relatedFacts: RBI launched the wholesale e-Rupee (e₹-W) pilot in November 2022 and retail e-Rupee (e₹-R) in December 2022.
CBDC is a sovereign legal tender represented digitally and appears as a liability on the central bank's balance sheet, unlike private cryptocurrencies.
Unlike bank deposits, holding physical cash or retail CBDC carries zero commercial bank credit risk.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.question: With reference to Infrastructure Investment Trusts (InvITs), consider the following statements:
statements: Interest income from the investments in InvITs which is distributed to their investors is exempt from tax, but the dividend income is taxable.
InvITs are recognized as borrowers under the 'Securitisation and Reconstruction of Financial Assets and Enforcement of Security Interest Act, 2002' (SARFAESI Act).
questions.concept: Tax pass-through status of collective investment trusts and SARFAESI borrowing powers.
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is incorrect: Under the Income Tax Act, 1961, the interest income distributed by an InvIT to its unit-holders is TAXABLE in the hands of the investor (following the pass-through mechanism), while dividend income distributed to unit-holders is generally EXEMPT if the Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) has not opted for the concessional corporate tax regime under Section 115BAA. The statement completely inverts the taxability. Statement 2 is correct: Under the 2021 amendments, InvITs and Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs) are explicitly recognized as 'borrowers' under the SARFAESI Act, 2002, empowering lenders to enforce security interests against them in case of default.

statementAnalysis.text: Interest income from the investments in InvITs which is distributed to their investors is exempt from tax, but the dividend income is taxable.
statementAnalysis.why: Inverts the tax provisions: interest income is taxable, while dividend income enjoys exemptions.

statementAnalysis.text: InvITs are recognized as borrowers under the 'Securitisation and Reconstruction of Financial Assets and Enforcement of Security Interest Act, 2002' (SARFAESI Act).
statementAnalysis.why: Enacted via the 2021 statutory amendment to SARFAESI.

optionAnalysis.a: Incorrect because statement 1 is false.
optionAnalysis.b: Correct: Only statement 2 is valid.
optionAnalysis.c: Incorrect because statement 1 is false.

questions.trap: Symmetric inversion of tax rules between dividend income and interest income.
relatedFacts: InvITs are regulated by SEBI under the SEBI (Infrastructure Investment Trusts) Regulations, 2014.
National Highways Infra Trust (NHIT) is the flagship InvIT of the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI).
InvITs pool small sums of money from retail and institutional investors to invest in revenue-generating infrastructure assets (toll roads, power transmission grids).

questions.subject: Economy
questions.question: With reference to the Indian economy, consider the following statements:
statements: An increase in Nominal Effective Exchange Rate (NEER) indicates the appreciation of rupee.
An increase in the Real Effective Exchange Rate (REER) indicates an improvement in trade competitiveness.
An increasing trend in domestic inflation relative to inflation in other countries is likely to cause an increasing divergence between NEER and REER.
questions.concept: Trade-weighted index of bilateral exchange rates adjusted for relative domestic vs foreign inflation differentials.
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is correct: NEER is a trade-weighted basket of bilateral nominal exchange rates. An increase in the NEER index denotes that the Indian Rupee has appreciated against the trade-weighted basket of partner currencies. Statement 2 is incorrect: REER = NEER adjusted for the relative price levels (inflation differentials). When REER increases (appreciates), domestic goods become relatively more expensive compared to foreign goods, which causes a DETERIORATION (loss) of export trade competitiveness, NOT an improvement. Statement 3 is correct: Since REER = NEER × (Domestic Price Index / Foreign Price Index), higher domestic inflation relative to trading partners directly widens the divergence between NEER and REER.

statementAnalysis.text: An increase in Nominal Effective Exchange Rate (NEER) indicates the appreciation of rupee.
statementAnalysis.why: NEER index increase directly signifies nominal currency appreciation.

statementAnalysis.text: An increase in the Real Effective Exchange Rate (REER) indicates an improvement in trade competitiveness.
statementAnalysis.why: A higher REER means domestic goods are pricier, eroding export competitiveness.

statementAnalysis.text: An increasing trend in domestic inflation relative to inflation in other countries is likely to cause an increasing divergence between NEER and REER.
statementAnalysis.why: Inflation differentials form the multiplier separating REER from NEER.

optionAnalysis.a: Incorrect because statement 2 is false.
optionAnalysis.b: Incorrect because statement 2 is false.
optionAnalysis.c: Correct option validating statements 1 and 3.

questions.trap: Assuming 'increase in REER' is good for trade; real currency appreciation actually makes exports uncompetitive.
relatedFacts: RBI computes both 40-currency and 6-currency baskets of NEER and REER with base year 2015-16.
A REER value above 100 indicates that the currency is overvalued in trade-weighted terms.
When domestic inflation exceeds foreign inflation, the currency must nominally depreciate to preserve constant real purchasing power (REER).

questions.subject: Economy
questions.question: In India, which one of the following is responsible for maintaining price stability by controlling inflation?
questions.concept: Statutory mandate of the central bank under Section 45ZA of the amended RBI Act, 1934.
questions.explanation: Under the 2016 statutory amendment to the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934, the primary objective of monetary policy is explicitly defined: 'to maintain price stability while keeping in mind the objective of growth'. The RESERVE BANK OF INDIA (through its Monetary Policy Committee) is the designated statutory authority legally responsible for controlling inflation and maintaining price stability around the 4% (+/- 2%) target.

optionAnalysis.a: Incorrect: Monitors retail commodity prices and weights/measures, not monetary policy.
optionAnalysis.b: Incorrect: Deals with rationalization of government expenditure.
optionAnalysis.c: Incorrect: FSDC deals with macro-prudential stability and financial sector development, chaired by Finance Minister.
optionAnalysis.d: Correct: Statutory sole mandate of the RBI.

questions.trap: Selecting government departments or councils instead of the Central Bank.
relatedFacts: If the RBI fails to meet the inflation target for three consecutive quarters, it must submit an explanatory report to the Central Government stating reasons, remedial actions, and estimated time to return to target.
FSDC is a non-statutory council set up in 2010 based on Raghuram Rajan Committee recommendations.
The Consumer Price Index (CPI-Combined) prepared by NSO is the anchor metric for inflation targeting.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.question: Which among the following steps is most likely to be taken at the time of an economic recession?

options.a: Cut in tax rates accompanied by increase in interest rate
options.b: Increase in expenditure on public projects
options.c: Increase in tax rates accompanied by reduction of interest rate
options.d: Reduction of expenditure on public projects

questions.concept: Keynesian expansionary pump-priming via public capital expenditure to revive aggregate demand.
questions.explanation: During an economic recession characterized by private investment stagnation and demand contraction, John Maynard Keynes advocated for Counter-Cyclical Fiscal Policy. The government steps in to 'pump-prime' the economy by INCREASING EXPENDITURE ON PUBLIC PROJECTS (infrastructure, roads, bridges). This stimulates employment, puts income into the hands of households, generates the fiscal multiplier effect, and crowding-in private investment.

optionAnalysis.a: Incorrect: Increasing interest rates is contractionary and will worsen recession.
optionAnalysis.b: Correct: Classic textbook counter-cyclical fiscal intervention.
optionAnalysis.c: Incorrect: Increasing tax rates dampens disposable income.

questions.trap: Contradictory options: Option (a) pairs tax cuts (expansionary) with interest rate hikes (contractionary).
relatedFacts: Counter-cyclical policy: Deficit spending in downturns, fiscal consolidation/surplus in economic booms.
The Economic Survey 2020-21 explicitly argued that counter-cyclical fiscal policy enables India to grow out of debt.
Capital expenditure (Capex) has a significantly higher multiplier (~2.45) compared to revenue expenditure (~0.98).

questions.subject: Economy
questions.question: Which of the following is/are the reason/reasons for considering Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) as a preferred form of foreign capital inflow over Foreign Portfolio Investment (FPI)?
statements: FDI brings along transfer of technology, management practices, and creates physical productive capacity.
FDI is non-debt creating and relatively stable, whereas FPI is volatile 'hot money' susceptible to rapid flight during global shocks.
questions.concept: Strategic long-term asset creation versus liquid, volatile financial instruments.
questions.explanation: Both statements are correct: Statement 1 is correct: FDI represents lasting interest and significant management control (usually 10% or more equity stake in an unlisted or listed company), bringing cutting-edge technology transfer, managerial expertise, global supply-chain integration, and greenfield physical assets. Statement 2 is correct: FDI is non-debt creating and represents long-term patient capital that cannot be liquidated overnight, whereas FPI (purchases of shares/bonds on stock exchanges) is highly liquid 'hot money' that can rapidly flee at the slightest change in US Federal Reserve interest rates or geopolitical tensions.

statementAnalysis.text: FDI brings along transfer of technology, management practices, and creates physical productive capacity.
statementAnalysis.why: Core economic rationale for attracting foreign direct investment.

statementAnalysis.text: FDI is non-debt creating and relatively stable, whereas FPI is volatile 'hot money' susceptible to rapid flight during global shocks.
statementAnalysis.why: FPI is liquid market trading; FDI is durable illiquid physical investment.

optionAnalysis.a: Incorrect because statement 2 is also valid.
optionAnalysis.b: Incorrect because statement 1 is also valid.
optionAnalysis.c: Correct option validating both fundamental economic truths.

questions.trap: Believing FPI is equally stable because it is regulated by SEBI.
relatedFacts: Arvind Mayaram Committee defined investment of 10% or more in a listed company as FDI, and less than 10% as FPI.
Singapore and Mauritius are historically the largest sources of FDI equity inflows into India.
External Commercial Borrowings (ECBs) and NRI deposits are debt-creating capital flows, whereas FDI and FPI are non-debt flows.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.question: With reference to the Indian economy, consider the following pairs of financial instruments:
statements: Commercial Paper (CP) — A short-term unsecured promissory note issued by corporations
Certificate of Deposit (CD) — A long-term debt instrument issued by the Reserve Bank of India
Call Money — A short-term finance used for interbank transactions
Zero-Coupon Bonds — The interest-bearing bonds issued by the Treasury
questions.concept: Issuers, tenors, and discount mechanisms of Indian money market instruments.
questions.explanation: Pair 1 is correctly matched: Commercial Paper is an unsecured short-term money market promissory note issued by highly rated corporates to raise working capital (maturity from 7 days to 1 year). Pair 2 is incorrectly matched: A Certificate of Deposit is a negotiable, short-term money market instrument issued by SCHEDULED COMMERCIAL BANKS and All-India Financial Institutions, NOT by the RBI. Pair 3 is correctly matched: Call Money is overnight interbank borrowing and lending to maintain CRR/SLR. Pair 4 is incorrectly matched: Zero-Coupon Bonds do NOT carry periodic interest (no coupons); they are issued at a deep discount to face value and redeemed at par (e.g. Treasury Bills).

statementAnalysis.text: Commercial Paper (CP) — A short-term unsecured promissory note issued by corporations
statementAnalysis.why: Introduced in India in 1990 for corporate working capital.

statementAnalysis.text: Certificate of Deposit (CD) — A long-term debt instrument issued by the Reserve Bank of India
statementAnalysis.why: Issued by commercial banks and financial institutions, not RBI; it is short-term.

statementAnalysis.text: Call Money — A short-term finance used for interbank transactions
statementAnalysis.why: 1-day overnight borrowing between commercial banks.

statementAnalysis.text: Zero-Coupon Bonds — The interest-bearing bonds issued by the Treasury
statementAnalysis.why: Zero-coupon implies zero interest payments; issued at discount and redeemed at par.

optionAnalysis.a: Incorrect because Pair 2 is false.
optionAnalysis.b: Incorrect because Pair 4 is false.
optionAnalysis.c: Correct answer containing Pairs 1 and 3.

questions.trap: Calling Zero-Coupon bonds 'interest-bearing' when by definition they pay ZERO coupon interest.
relatedFacts: Notice Money refers to funds borrowed for 2 to 14 days; Term Money refers to funds borrowed for 15 days to 1 year.
Treasury Bills (T-Bills) in India are issued by the Government of India through RBI in three tenors: 91 days, 182 days, and 364 days.
State Governments in India do NOT issue Treasury Bills; they issue State Development Loans (SDLs).

questions.subject: Economy
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding 'Capital Adequacy Ratio' (CAR):
statements: CAR is the amount that banks have to maintain in the form of their own funds to offset any loss that banks incur if the account-holders fail to repay dues.
CAR is decided by each bank individually without any uniform mandate.
questions.subTopic: Basel Accords & Capital to Risk-Weighted Assets Ratio (CRAR)
questions.concept: Regulatory capital buffer protecting depositors against asset default shocks.
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is correct: Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR), also known as Capital-to-Risk Weighted Assets Ratio (CRAR), is the ratio of a bank's capital (Tier 1 core capital + Tier 2 supplementary capital) to its risk-weighted assets. It serves as an equity cushion to absorb unexpected loan default losses and protect depositors. Statement 2 is incorrect: CAR is NOT decided by individual banks; it is strictly regulated and mandated by Central Banks under the international Basel Norms (Basel Committee on Banking Supervision). In India, RBI prescribes a minimum CAR of 9% for scheduled commercial banks (higher than the Basel III minimum of 8%).

statementAnalysis.text: CAR is the amount that banks have to maintain in the form of their own funds to offset any loss that banks incur if the account-holders fail to repay dues.
statementAnalysis.why: Core prudential objective of capital adequacy.

statementAnalysis.text: CAR is decided by each bank individually without any uniform mandate.
statementAnalysis.why: Mandated by RBI based on Basel Accords.

optionAnalysis.a: Correct: Only statement 1 is factually and economically sound.
optionAnalysis.b: Incorrect because statement 2 is false.
optionAnalysis.c: Incorrect because statement 2 is false.

questions.trap: Believing commercial banks have individual autonomy over solvency and safety metrics.
relatedFacts: Tier 1 capital consists primarily of common equity and retained earnings (gone-concern loss absorber).
Tier 2 capital consists of subordinated debt, revaluation reserves, and general loan-loss provisions.
Basel III framework introduced the Capital Conservation Buffer (CCB) of 2.5% and Countercyclical Capital Buffer (CCCB).

questions.subject: Economy
questions.question: Which of the following activities of the Reserve Bank of India is considered to be part of 'sterilization'?

options.b: Oversight of settlement and payment systems
options.c: Debt and cash management for the Central and State Governments
options.d: Regulating the functions of Non-Banking Financial Institutions

questions.concept: Mechanisms by which the central bank insulates domestic money supply from foreign exchange interventions.
questions.explanation: Sterilization refers to the operations undertaken by a central bank (RBI) to neutralize the effects of its intervention in the foreign exchange market on the domestic monetary base. When large foreign capital inflows occur, the RBI buys foreign currency (US Dollars) to prevent sharp Rupee appreciation, which injects equivalent domestic liquidity (Rupees) into the banking system. To prevent this excess liquidity from igniting inflation, the RBI conducts Open Market Operations (OMO)—selling government securities to absorb the newly created Rupees. Hence, Open Market Operations are the primary instrument of sterilization.

optionAnalysis.a: Correct: OMO sale of government securities absorbs domestic liquidity pumped in by buying foreign currencies.
optionAnalysis.b: Incorrect: Oversight of payment systems is a routine regulatory mandate under the PSS Act, 2007.
optionAnalysis.c: Incorrect: Government debt and cash management is RBI's role as banker to the government.
optionAnalysis.d: Incorrect: NBFC regulation is prudential micro-supervision, unrelated to monetary sterilization.

questions.trap: Candidates confuse sterilization (which is purely a macroeconomic liquidity management mechanism) with regulatory or sanitization procedures.
relatedFacts: The Market Stabilization Scheme (MSS) was introduced in 2004 specifically to provide the RBI with dedicated securities for sterilization.
Unsterilized intervention directly increases reserve money (M0) and can induce demand-pull inflation.
Sterilization carries quasi-fiscal costs because the yield earned on foreign reserve assets is generally lower than the interest paid on domestic sterilization bonds.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.question: With reference to the Indian economy, what are the advantages of 'Inflation-Indexed Bonds' (IIBs)?
statements: Government can reduce the coupon rates on its borrowing by way of IIBs.
IIBs provide protection to the investors from uncertainty regarding inflation.
The interest received as well as capital gains on IIBs are not subjected to taxation.
questions.concept: Design, risk-mitigation features, and tax treatment of sovereign inflation-indexed debt instruments.
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is correct: Since investors are compensated for inflation through principal indexation, governments do not need to offer high nominal risk premiums, allowing lower coupon rates. Statement 2 is correct: The fundamental raison d'être of IIBs is to protect investors' principal and interest from inflation erosion (pegged to CPI or WPI). Statement 3 is incorrect: There is no special tax exemption for IIBs in India; the interest received is treated as ordinary income and subject to income tax, and capital gains are taxed per existing capital gains tax provisions.

statementAnalysis.text: Government can reduce the coupon rates on its borrowing by way of IIBs.
statementAnalysis.why: Eliminates the inflation risk premium required by lenders, lowering nominal coupon yields.

statementAnalysis.text: IIBs provide protection to the investors from uncertainty regarding inflation.
statementAnalysis.why: Principal value is indexed directly to the inflation index (CPI), shielding real returns.

statementAnalysis.text: The interest received as well as capital gains on IIBs are not subjected to taxation.
statementAnalysis.why: Interest and capital gains are subject to standard income tax and capital gains tax rules.

optionAnalysis.a: Correct: Statements 1 and 2 are true, while Statement 3 is false.
optionAnalysis.b: Incorrect: Statement 3 is false.
optionAnalysis.c: Incorrect: Statement 3 is false.

questions.trap: Aspirants assume government-backed public welfare/inflation bonds are tax-free like tax-free infrastructure bonds.
relatedFacts: RBI launched Capital Indexed Bonds (CIBs) in 1997, and revamped them as Inflation-Indexed Bonds (IIBs) in 2013.
In IIBs, inflation adjustment is applied to the principal, and coupon payments are calculated on the adjusted principal.
IIBs incentivize domestic financial savings rather than hoarding physical gold as an inflation hedge.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.question: With reference to the Indian economy, consider the following statements regarding WPI and CPI:
statements: The weightage of food in Consumer Price Index (CPI) is higher than that in Wholesale Price Index (WPI).
The WPI does not capture changes in the prices of services, which CPI does.
Reserve Bank of India has now adopted WPI as its key measure of inflation and to decide on changing the key policy rates.
questions.subTopic: Wholesale Price Index (WPI) vs Consumer Price Index (CPI)
questions.concept: Methodological differences, basket composition, weights, and institutional adoption between WPI and CPI.
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is correct: The weight of food and beverages in CPI (Combined) is 45.86%, whereas in WPI the weight of primary food articles and manufactured food products combined is approximately 24.38%. Statement 2 is correct: WPI covers only physical commodities/goods (Manufactured Products, Primary Articles, Fuel & Power) and completely excludes services. CPI covers both goods and services (education, medical care, transport, communication). Statement 3 is incorrect: Following the Urjit Patel Committee recommendations in 2014, the RBI officially discarded WPI and adopted CPI (Combined) headline inflation as the sole nominal anchor for monetary policy targeting (4% +/- 2%).

statementAnalysis.text: The weightage of food in Consumer Price Index (CPI) is higher than that in Wholesale Price Index (WPI).
statementAnalysis.why: Food weight is ~45.86% in CPI compared to ~24.4% in WPI.

statementAnalysis.text: The WPI does not capture changes in the prices of services, which CPI does.
statementAnalysis.why: WPI tracks wholesale goods at the factory gate; services are strictly tracked by CPI.

statementAnalysis.text: Reserve Bank of India has now adopted WPI as its key measure of inflation and to decide on changing the key policy rates.
statementAnalysis.why: RBI switched from WPI to CPI (Combined) headline inflation in 2014 under Flexible Inflation Targeting.

optionAnalysis.a: Correct: Statements 1 and 2 accurately capture the technical and policy distinctions.
optionAnalysis.b: Incorrect: Omits correct statement 1.
optionAnalysis.c: Incorrect: Statement 3 is false.

questions.trap: Examiner reverses the monetary anchor: RBI previously used WPI (prior to 2014), but currently uses CPI.
relatedFacts: WPI is published monthly by the Office of the Economic Adviser, Ministry of Commerce and Industry (Base year 2011-12).
CPI is released monthly by the National Statistical Office (NSO), Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) (Base year 2012).
Under Section 45ZA of the RBI Act, 1934, the Central Government in consultation with RBI sets the inflation target based on Consumer Price Index (Combined).

questions.subject: Economy
questions.question: Which of the following factors/policies were affecting the price of rice in India in the recent past?
statements: Minimum Support Price
Government's trading
Government's stockpiling
Consumer subsidies
questions.subTopic: Price Determination & State Intervention in Foodgrain Markets
questions.concept: Multi-channel impact of government procurement, buffer stocking, open market sales, and PDS subsidies on market equilibrium prices.
questions.explanation: All four factors affect the domestic price of rice in India: 1. Minimum Support Price (MSP) acts as an effective floor price in grain markets, influencing private market rates. 2. Government's trading (Open Market Sale Scheme - OMSS, export bans, tariffs) alters the supply-demand balance in wholesale markets. 3. Government's stockpiling by the Food Corporation of India (FCI) absorbs physical surplus during harvest seasons and releases it during lean periods, directly moderating market price volatility. 4. Consumer subsidies through the National Food Security Act (NFSA) and Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana (PMGKAY) distribute highly subsidized or free grains, dampening open market demand.

statementAnalysis.text: Minimum Support Price
statementAnalysis.why: Establishes a statutory floor benchmark for procurement.

statementAnalysis.text: Government's trading
statementAnalysis.why: Direct OMSS tenders and trade restrictions alter supply elasticities.

statementAnalysis.text: Government's stockpiling
statementAnalysis.why: FCI buffer stock operations absorb market gluts and release supplies.

statementAnalysis.text: Consumer subsidies
statementAnalysis.why: Public distribution under NFSA depresses open market retail demand.

optionAnalysis.a: Incorrect: Excludes stockpiling.
optionAnalysis.b: Incorrect: Excludes government trading.
optionAnalysis.c: Incorrect: Excludes MSP and subsidies.
optionAnalysis.d: Correct: All four state interventions influence the equilibrium price of rice.

questions.trap: Aspirants mistakenly assume consumer subsidies only affect consumers' wallets without recognizing how they shift the market demand curve.
relatedFacts: CACP (Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices) recommends MSPs based on A2+FL and C2 cost formulations.
FCI is the nodal agency for procurement, storage, and movement of foodgrains across India.
India is the world's largest exporter of rice, accounting for ~40% of global rice trade.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.question: What is the importance of developing the Chabahar Port by India?

options.a: India's trade with African countries will enormously increase.
options.b: India's relations with oil-producing Arab countries will be strengthened.
options.c: India will not depend on Pakistan for access to Afghanistan and Central Asia.
options.d: Pakistan will facilitate and protect the installation of a gas pipeline between Iraq and India.

questions.concept: Strategic bypass of overland transit barriers to Afghanistan and the INSTC corridor.
questions.explanation: Chabahar Port, located in the Sistan-Baluchistan province on Iran's southeastern coast (Gulf of Oman), provides India with a direct oceanic and multimodal gateway to Afghanistan and the resource-rich Central Asian Republics (CAR), completely bypassing Pakistan, which historically denied overland transit rights to Indian commercial goods. It connects to the Zaranj-Delaram highway in Afghanistan built by India's Border Roads Organisation (BRO).

optionAnalysis.a: Incorrect: Chabahar is in Iran (West Asia), not on African maritime trade routes.
optionAnalysis.b: Incorrect: Iran is a Persian, non-Arab nation; Chabahar is outside the Persian Gulf.
optionAnalysis.c: Correct: Circumvents Pakistani overland transit denial, providing direct sea-land access to Afghanistan and Central Asia.

questions.trap: Candidates confuse the geographic and demographic profile of Iran (Persian/Shia) with Arab Gulf countries.
relatedFacts: India operates the Shahid Beheshti terminal at Chabahar Port through India Ports Global Limited (IPGL).
Chabahar is a vital node in the International North-South Transport Corridor (INSTC).
Chabahar is located less than 100 km west of Pakistan's Gwadar port, developed under China's CPEC.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding the Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management (FRBM) Review Committee Report:
statements: The FRBM Review Committee (N.K. Singh Committee) recommended a debt-to-GDP ratio of 60% for the general (combined) government by 2023, comprising 40% for Central Government and 20% for State Governments.
The Central Government has domestic liabilities of 21% of GDP as compared to that of 49% of GDP of the State Governments.
As per the Constitution of India, it is mandatory for a State to take the Central Government's consent for raising any loan if the State has any outstanding liabilities to the Centre.
questions.subTopic: FRBM Act & N.K. Singh Review Committee
questions.concept: Prudential debt targets, constitutional borrowing limits under Article 293, and central vs state debt dynamics.
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is correct: The N.K. Singh FRBM Review Committee recommended transitioning from fiscal deficit targeting to a debt-to-GDP target: 60% combined debt-to-GDP ratio by FY2023 (40% Centre, 20% States). Statement 2 is incorrect: The figures are inverted; the Centre's debt is significantly higher (~49-55% of GDP) than the combined States' debt (~21-28% of GDP). Statement 3 is correct: Under Article 293(3) of the Constitution of India, a State may not without the consent of the Government of India raise any loan if there is still outstanding any part of a loan which has been made to the State by the Government of India.

statementAnalysis.text: The FRBM Review Committee (N.K. Singh Committee) recommended a debt-to-GDP ratio of 60% for the general (combined) government by 2023, comprising 40% for Central Government and 20% for State Governments.
statementAnalysis.why: Exact recommendation of the 2017 N.K. Singh Committee.

statementAnalysis.text: The Central Government has domestic liabilities of 21% of GDP as compared to that of 49% of GDP of the State Governments.
statementAnalysis.why: Centre holds the majority of sovereign debt (~50%), while States hold ~25-28%.

statementAnalysis.text: As per the Constitution of India, it is mandatory for a State to take the Central Government's consent for raising any loan if the State has any outstanding liabilities to the Centre.
statementAnalysis.why: Direct mandate of Article 293(3) of the Constitution.

optionAnalysis.a: Incorrect: Statement 3 is also correct.
optionAnalysis.b: Incorrect: Statement 2 is false.
optionAnalysis.c: Correct: Statements 1 and 3 are correct.

questions.trap: Examiner flipped the liability percentages between Centre and States in Statement 2 to test factual precision.
relatedFacts: Article 292 governs borrowing by the Government of India, while Article 293 governs borrowing by States.
States cannot raise loans outside India under any circumstances (borrowing must be within the territory of India).
The N.K. Singh committee also introduced 'Escape Clauses' allowing a 0.5% deviation from fiscal deficit targets during national emergencies, war, or agricultural collapses.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.question: Which of the following has/have occurred in India after its liberalization of economic policies in 1991?
statements: Share of agriculture in GDP increased enormously.
Share of India's exports in world trade increased.
FDI inflows increased.
India's foreign exchange reserves increased enormously.
questions.concept: Structural transformation of the Indian macroeconomy post-1991 reforms.
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is incorrect: The share of agriculture in India's GDP has consistently declined post-1991 (from over 30% in 1991 to under 18% in recent years), while the services sector expanded rapidly. Statement 2 is correct: India's share in world merchandise and service exports grew from ~0.5% in 1991 to over 2% post-reforms. Statement 3 is correct: Opening up of automatic and government approval routes resulted in exponential surges in Foreign Direct Investment (FDI). Statement 4 is correct: India's forex reserves climbed from a precarious $1.2 billion in 1991 (barely 2 weeks of imports) to well over $600 billion.

statementAnalysis.text: Share of agriculture in GDP increased enormously.
statementAnalysis.why: Agriculture's GDP share declined as services and industry expanded.

statementAnalysis.text: Share of India's exports in world trade increased.
statementAnalysis.why: Global trade integration boosted India's share of world exports.

statementAnalysis.text: FDI inflows increased.
statementAnalysis.why: FDI caps were dismantled across manufacturing, telecom, and services.

statementAnalysis.text: India's foreign exchange reserves increased enormously.
statementAnalysis.why: Forex reserves expanded from $1.2 billion in 1991 to over $600 billion.

optionAnalysis.a: Incorrect: Statement 1 is false.
optionAnalysis.b: Correct: Statements 2, 3, and 4 represent undisputed macroeconomic facts.
optionAnalysis.c: Incorrect: Excludes Statement 4.

questions.trap: A common mistake is confusing absolute agricultural production (which increased) with agriculture's percentage share in GDP (which sharply declined).
relatedFacts: The 1991 reforms abolished the Industrial Licensing system ('Licence Raj') for all but a few strategic sectors.
The Rupee was made fully convertible on the Current Account in August 1994, but remains partially convertible on the Capital Account.
Tariff barriers dropped dramatically: peak customs duties fell from over 300% in 1991 to under 10% for non-agricultural goods.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.question: What is/are the purpose/purposes of Government's 'Sovereign Gold Bond Scheme' and 'Gold Monetisation Scheme'?
statements: To bring the idle gold lying with Indian households and institutions into the financial system.
To promote FDI in the gold and jewellery sector.
To reduce India's dependence on gold imports.
questions.concept: Policy objectives to curb the Current Account Deficit (CAD) by replacing physical gold demand with paper instruments.
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 3 are correct: The Sovereign Gold Bond (SGB) Scheme and Gold Monetisation Scheme (GMS) were launched in November 2015 to mobilize idle gold held by households and institutions and to shift physical investment demand into paper gold, thereby reducing high gold imports that widened the Current Account Deficit (CAD). Statement 2 is incorrect: The schemes have nothing to do with promoting FDI in the gold and jewellery sector.

statementAnalysis.text: To bring the idle gold lying with Indian households and institutions into the financial system.
statementAnalysis.why: GMS enables depositors to earn interest on idle physical ornaments and bars.

statementAnalysis.text: To promote FDI in the gold and jewellery sector.
statementAnalysis.why: Schemes are focused on macroeconomic CAD reduction, not FDI promotion.

statementAnalysis.text: To reduce India's dependence on gold imports.
statementAnalysis.why: Replacing physical bar/coin purchases with paper SGBs directly saves foreign exchange.

optionAnalysis.a: Incorrect: Statement 3 is also an explicit objective.
optionAnalysis.b: Incorrect: Statement 2 is false.
optionAnalysis.c: Correct: Statements 1 and 3 are the twin primary objectives.

questions.trap: Examiners frequently slip in 'promote FDI' into domestic micro-savings and gold mobilization schemes.
relatedFacts: SGBs are issued by the RBI on behalf of the Government of India under the Government Securities Act, 2006.
SGBs offer an annual fixed interest rate (typically 2.50%) payable semi-annually on nominal value.
Capital gains tax arising on redemption of SGB to an individual is completely exempted from income tax.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.question: Which one of the following best describes the term 'Merchant Discount Rate' (MDR)?

options.a: The rate at which a commercial bank borrows money from the RBI against government securities.
options.b: The discount offered by a merchant to a customer on making payments through digital modes.
options.c: The fee charged by a bank to a merchant for accepting payments from his customers via credit/debit cards.
options.d: The incentive given by the Government to merchants for promoting digital payments through UPI.

questions.concept: Fee structure and economics of digital payment acquiring infrastructure.
questions.explanation: Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) is the fee that a merchant pays to the acquiring bank that processes transactions from payment cards (credit cards, debit cards, point-of-sale machines). This fee is shared among the acquiring bank, the card-issuing bank (interchange fee), and the payment network (e.g., Visa, Mastercard, RuPay). In 2020, the Government of India waived MDR on RuPay debit cards and UPI transactions to accelerate financial inclusion and cashless transactions.

optionAnalysis.a: Incorrect: Describes Repo Rate.
optionAnalysis.b: Incorrect: Confuses the fee with a commercial merchant cashback/discount.
optionAnalysis.c: Correct: The charge paid by a merchant to the bank for digital payment processing services.
optionAnalysis.d: Incorrect: That represents government reimbursement subsidies, not MDR itself.

questions.trap: The word 'Discount' misleads aspirants into thinking it is a retail consumer rebate rather than a transactional merchant fee.
relatedFacts: The Reserve Bank of India regulates MDR caps under the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007.
Zero MDR on UPI and RuPay led to meteoric adoption across small tea stalls and kirana stores across India.
The RBI established the Payments Infrastructure Development Fund (PIDF) to subsidize PoS deployment in Tier-3 to Tier-6 centers.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.question: With reference to the Indian Financial Sector, what is the role of an 'Account Aggregator' (AA)?
statements: It acts as a financial entity that collects financial data from Financial Information Providers (FIP) and shares it with Financial Information Users (FIU) with explicit customer consent.
It is allowed to view, store, or sell the customer's financial data to third-party marketing companies.
questions.concept: RBI-regulated Non-Banking Financial Company - Account Aggregator (NBFC-AA) framework.
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is correct: An Account Aggregator (AA) is an RBI-regulated entity (NBFC-AA) that facilitates encrypted, consent-based financial data sharing between Financial Information Providers (FIPs—e.g. banks, mutual funds, insurance) and Financial Information Users (FIUs—e.g. lenders, wealth managers). Statement 2 is incorrect: An AA is strictly 'data-blind'; it operates on a zero-knowledge architecture. The data passing through the AA is end-to-end encrypted; the AA CANNOT view, decrypt, store, or monetize customer financial records.

statementAnalysis.text: It acts as a financial entity that collects financial data from Financial Information Providers (FIP) and shares it with Financial Information Users (FIU) with explicit customer consent.
statementAnalysis.why: Core statutory function defined under RBI's NBFC-AA Master Directions.

statementAnalysis.text: It is allowed to view, store, or sell the customer's financial data to third-party marketing companies.
statementAnalysis.why: AAs are prohibited from reading, storing, or monetizing unencrypted customer financial data.

optionAnalysis.a: Correct: Only Statement 1 accurately captures the AA architecture.
optionAnalysis.b: Incorrect: Statement 2 is false.
optionAnalysis.c: Incorrect: Statement 2 is false.

questions.trap: Candidates assume digital intermediaries can access or store data like traditional credit rating agencies or data brokers.
relatedFacts: The AA framework is part of the India Stack (Data Empowerment and Protection Architecture - DEPA).
Cross-sector financial regulators (RBI, SEBI, IRDAI, PFRDA) have integrated their regulated entities into the AA network.
Enables instant collateral-free cash-flow-based lending for MSMEs without physical paper bank statements.
